item.title: Kerry Gardaí have stopped motorists who’ve been watching matches while driving
item.description: A Kerry Roads Policing Unit inspector says they've stopped people watching soccer and soap operas on their mobile phone while driving. Increased checkpoints are taking place throughout Kerry this bank holiday weekend and there'll be an increased focus on distracted drivers. Inspector Gary Carroll says while the vast majority of motorists heed their messages, there is a small percentage of people who engage in dangerous behaviours on our roads. item.title: Djokovic through to 11th Australian Open final
item.description: Novak Djokovic is through to an 11th Australian Open tennis final after getting past defending champion Yannik Sinner in five sets. The Serb remains on course for a record 25th Grand Slam singles title in Melbourne. Djokovic will face world number one Carlos Alcaraz, who overcame cramp to fight back in a five-set thriller lasting almost five-and-a-half hours against German Alexander Zverev. Advertisement

item.title: Leopardstown passes track inspection
item.description: Leopardstown has passed a track inspection this afternoon, on the eve of the Dublin Racing Festival. 22 millimetres of rain overnight has brought the two-week total to 193mm, leaving sections of the hurdle course unfit for racing once again. Another inspection will take place tomorrow morning at 8 o'clock, before a seven-race card due to get underway at quarter-past-1. Advertisement

item.title: Tralee Bay Wetlands to mark World Wetlands Day 2026
item.description: Tralee Bay Wetlands will mark the annual World Wetlands Day on February 2nd. It celebrates the habitats ecological value, and role it plays in supporting biodiversity climate resilience, and cultural heritage. Tralee Bay Wetlands will hold a series of events to mark the occasion, including workshops, talks, a marsh walk and bird watching. item.title: Rovers confirm signing of teenage winger Adam Brennan
item.description: Shamrock Rovers have confirmed the signing of teenage winger Adam Brennan for the upcoming season. The 18-year-old joins from UCD, where he became the first player to progress through every level of the academy to the senior team. Brennan scored nine goals and provided twelve assists in the First Division last season and has already represented Ireland at under-19 level. Advertisement

item.title: President Catherine Connolly tells Ballybunion event she'd like to live here in Kerry
item.description: The President of Ireland Catherine Connolly has told an event in Ballybunion that she would love to live here in Kerry. She was speaking at ‘What if We Were Brilliant’, a celebration event to mark the culmination of a community-led, climate action initiative by the Brilliant Ballybunion group. Over the last two years, the initiative has focused on growing food, being creative, and protecting nature, and was funded through the Creative Climate Action Fund. item.title: Allianz League fixtures hit by venue changes
item.description: A number of Allianz League fixtures this weekend have been hit by venue changes due to Storm Chandra and ongoing wet conditions. Heavy rain and localised flooding have caused several pitches to be deemed unplayable, with weather warnings still in place this evening. In Division Two, Louth’s clash with Cork has been moved from Ardee to the Integral GAA Grounds in Drogheda.
